name: Derivative
description: A derivative is a financial contract involving two or more parties that can be traded either on an exchange or directly between parties (over-the-counter, OTC). These agreements allow for the trading of various assets and come with inherent risks. The value of derivatives is based on changes in the price of the underlying asset. Commonly employed to engage with specific markets, derivatives are used either to reduce risk (hedging) or to take on risk in hopes of achieving proportional gains (speculation).

name: Wrapped Token
description: A wrapped token is a tokenized representation of a cryptocurrency (such as Bitcoin or Ethereum) on a different blockchain network. It allows non-native assets to be used across decentralized applications (dApps), decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, and smart contracts on other chains. Wrapped tokens are typically backed 1:1 by the original asset, which is securely held by a custodian or controlled through a smart contract. The process of wrapping and unwrapping may be governed by centralized or decentralized systems, depending on the protocol. Wrapped tokens are essential for cross-chain interoperability, enabling users to leverage assets like BTC on networks such as Ethereum, BNB Chain, or Solana without leaving the ecosystem of the original coin.
